provenance.purpose: Every consumer-visible rename the v1 absorption makes, recorded as it happens.
provenance.rule: A batch that renames anything a consumer can import, target or reference owes a row here, in the same PR. The batch plan lists the rows each batch owes.

schema.kind: component | export | class | token | path | dependency — what is being renamed
schema.to: the 1.0 name, or null when the thing is removed with no replacement
schema.batch: the batch number that made the change
schema.note: optional — why, or what a consumer has to do beyond a find-and-replace
schema.notes: A change a consumer can see that is not yet a rename — recorded so the row it will owe later is not lost. Not read by the generator.

renames.note: Value corrected #89fc79 -> #53ff64. The 0.11 hex was eye-dropped from the charter PNG on the belief that the swatch label was a typo; the label was right. Name unchanged — re-check any hard-coded copy of the old hex.

Data series no longer read the themeable accent. Visually identical at the default theme (--ds-chart-1 is #ff2a00); a theme that overrode --ds-accent to recolour its charts must now override --ds-chart-*.

The geometric construction 0.x drew — a circle, a square and a diagonal line, the brand's three elements as primitives — is replaced by the produced lockups, as two `currentColor` variants: `horizontal` (the full name) and `square` (the monogram). `name` and `sub` are unchanged and still render `.ds-wordmark__name` / `__sub`, but they no longer default: a bare <Wordmark /> is now the lockup alone, where it used to print the word "Diametral". A name beside the mark wants variant="square" — the horizontal lockup already spells it. `.ds-wordmark__mark` still styles a hand-written svg; the React binding emits none. `assets/logo/diametral-mark.svg` still holds the geometric mark and has not been re-cut to match.

File move only, no rename and no visual change — the four rules left app-bar.css for the new wordmark.css when the real lockup landed. Anyone importing css/diametral.css is unaffected; only a consumer cherry-picking css/components/app-bar.css has to add css/components/wordmark.css.

Replaced wholesale, same name. The seam no longer overlaps members with margin-left: -1px; it removes the losing border with border-inline-start-width, which is identical in LTR and correct in RTL. Every selector matches both the new parts' data-slot and .ds-button/.ds-input/.ds-select, so existing markup keeps joining. New: [data-orientation="vertical"], .ds-button-group-text and .ds-button-group-separator.

Additive, not a rename: `sm` and `lg` keep working, and `icon-` is simply stripped, so the source's four square spellings resolve onto the same boxes. `icon-xs` (24px, .ds-button--xs) is new. `label` was already required on both sides — the ledger's "incumbent is a class-applier" premise does not hold here, the same way batch-plan §1.1 found for stat-card. Moved from react/components/ButtonExtras.tsx to react/components/icon-button.tsx; the barrel import is unchanged.

Renamed with the absorption; every prop survives (`value`, `max`, `size`, `thickness`, `label`, `color`, `thresholds`, `format`) and the props interface is gone in favour of the inline type, the way every absorbed component declares its props. A find-and-replace of the symbol is the whole migration.

renames.from: LineChart ({ series, data, labels, width, height })
renames.note: Recharts replaced the hand-rolled SVG, so a series is named and coloured once in `config` — one entry per key in each `data` row — and the rows are objects rather than parallel arrays. `labels` becomes `xAxisKey`, the row field holding them; `width`/`height` become the container's box (`.ds-chart-container--plot`, retuned with `--ds-chart-height`). `grid` and `dots` are unchanged. Same for AreaChart, which additionally gains `stacked`.

renames.from: AreaChart ({ series, data, labels, width, height })
renames.note: See LineChart. `stacked` is new: two areas drawn over each other are usually meant to sum.

renames.to: BarChart ({ config, data, xAxisKey, statusKey, max, horizontal, stacked })
renames.note: 0.11 took one array of `{ label, value, status }`; the rows are now recharts rows and the measure is a `config` key. `status` moves from the datum to `statusKey`, a row field naming the tone, and all six 0.11 tones survive (success, warning, danger, critical, neutral, info) — the source's own map had only four. `horizontal` and `max` keep their 0.11 names and meaning. BarChartDatum is gone.

Still the share chart: each row is normalised to its own total. `segments` and their colours become `config`; the row label becomes `labelKey`. For raw magnitudes rather than shares, use BarChart with `stacked`.

renames.to: PieChart ({ config, data, valueKey, nameKey, legend })
renames.note: `valueKey`/`nameKey` name the row fields; a slice's colour is a `config` entry keyed by its name, which is also how the tooltip and legend find its label. `size` becomes the container's square box — retune it with `--ds-chart-height`.

renames.from: DonutChart ({ data, centerLabel, thickness, legend, size })
renames.to: DonutChart ({ config, data, valueKey, nameKey, centerLabel, centerCaption, thickness, legend })
renames.note: See PieChart. `thickness` is now a percentage of the chart radius, not px, because the container is responsive and a px ring would not scale with it. `centerCaption` is new: the uppercase line under the figure, in the register Gauge uses.

renames.from: Sparkline (flat series drawn along the floor)
renames.to: Sparkline (flat series pinned to the middle)
renames.note: Props are unchanged. The one behavioural change is a defect fix: 0.11 divided by a `|| 1` span, so a flat series — or a single point — drew along the bottom of the box and read as a minimum it was not. It now pins to the vertical middle.

The chart merge: charts.css and bar-chart.css were deleted and the source's chart.css landed in their place. The wrapper survives as .ds-chart-container; the svg, gridlines and axis labels do not, because recharts generates those nodes itself and they cannot carry a ds-* class. chart.css restyles them through `.ds-chart-container .recharts-*` descendant rules instead. A hand-written static chart has no replacement markup — the axis charts are React-only from 1.0.0-beta.4 on. `.ds-sparkline` and `.ds-gauge` are the two that stay library-free.
Rename only; the swatch is still a 10px square. `.ds-chart-legend__value` has no replacement — the source's legend carries a label, not a label plus a figure.
Removed with the chart merge. Print the figure in the tooltip (`.ds-chart-tooltip-content-item-value`), or beside the chart as prose.
Removed with the chart merge: the marks are recharts <path> nodes now, styled per series from `config` rather than by class. There is no static markup that reproduces them.

Removed with the chart merge (bar-chart.css deleted). The CSS-flex bar chart — inline height/width percentages and `.is-success`-style tones on the bar — is replaced by recharts marks; the tone axis survives as BarChart's `statusKey`.
Only the root survives, and its job is now the box: full width, `--ds-chart-height` tall. The row, label, track and segments are recharts nodes.

Only the root survives (it centres the chart). The surface-coloured 1px seam between slices moved into chart.css, as `.ds-chart-container .recharts-sector[stroke="#fff"]` — recharts hard-codes a white hairline and the rule repaints it.

The ring itself is a recharts <Pie> now, so the track and the segments are gone. The two centre text classes survive under new names: `__center` (the figure) is `-center-label`, and `__center-label` (the caption under it) is `-center-caption` — the old pair read backwards.

Flat-kebab rename, no structural change: the gauge stays library-free, so hand-written markup keeps working after a find-and-replace of `__` for `-`. `.ds-gauge` itself is unchanged, and the value arc's transition is now a CSS declaration rather than an inline style.

Flat-kebab rename, no structural change; the sparkline stays library-free. `.ds-sparkline` keeps its `color: var(--ds-chart-1)` default, so an inline sparkline still paints from the series ramp rather than the accent.
The modifier moved from the root onto the polyline, which is the element the keyframe draws. The keyframe and its reduced-motion opt-out stay in components/motion.css.

renames.from: (none — height was a Tailwind class in the source)
renames.note: The knob that replaced the source's `h-56`/`h-64`/`h-40`/`h-24` literals. `.ds-chart-container--plot` and `--square` read it, defaulting to 14rem and 16rem; set it on the chart to retune one. This package has no Tailwind and no tailwind-merge, so a competing height class would be decided by stylesheet order — a variable is not.

Anyone importing css/diametral.css is unaffected. A consumer cherry-picking the two old files has to swap them for the five new ones (and keep css/components/sparkline.css, which was already separate).

renames.from: (none — the label and value column widths were Tailwind arbitrary-property classes in the source)
renames.note: The knobs that replaced the source's `[--bullet-label:7rem]` / `[--bullet-value:4rem]` literals on BulletChart's own className. `.ds-bullet-chart` declares both as its defaults and reads them in `grid-template-columns`; set either on the chart or on a wrapper to retune one bullet or a whole stack. Unprefixed `--bullet-*` is not read — every custom property in this package is `--ds-*`.

The sequential ramp `.ds-heatmap` quantises into, one hue getting darker. Separate from the categorical `--ds-chart-*` ramp on purpose: reading a categorical ramp as a scale is the classic dataviz error. It is also the one Tier-1 primitive css/themes/dark.css overrides — a sequential ramp encodes magnitude, so "more" has to mean brighter on a dark page. A theme that recolours data now has two ramps to consider, not one.
Renamed with the split into parts. `icon`/`title`/`description`/`actions` become <EmptyMedia>, <EmptyTitle>, <EmptyDescription> and <EmptyContent>, all inside an <EmptyHeader> except the content.
Base UI's Avatar. The fallback now appears only once the image has actually failed or is still loading; `size` survives and lands as data-size.
The overflow count is written rather than computed: `max` is gone and <AvatarGroupCount>+N</AvatarGroupCount> is the tail.

renames.to: Breadcrumb + BreadcrumbList + BreadcrumbItem + BreadcrumbLink + BreadcrumbPage + BreadcrumbSeparator + BreadcrumbEllipsis
renames.note: BreadcrumbLink is polymorphic through `render`, so a router's Link renders in its place with no wrapper.

renames.to: PageHeader + PageHeaderHeading + PageHeaderTitle + PageHeaderDescription + PageHeaderActions + PageHeaderIcon + PageHeaderTabs
renames.note: `flush` has no replacement: page-header.css derives it from `:has([data-slot=page-header-tabs])`, so the markup says it.

renames.to: Pagination + PaginationContent + PaginationItem + PaginationLink + PaginationNext + PaginationPrevious + PaginationEllipsis + paginationRange
renames.note: No capability is lost: `paginationRange({ page, pageCount, siblingCount })` is the same window function, exported. Rebuilding the controlled pager is ~10 lines and is written out in from-0.11.md. What the parts buy is a page that can be a real <a href>.
Base UI's Progress. `status` is spelled `tone` and takes six values; `indeterminate` is `value={null}`; `label` is a <ProgressLabel> child.
`label` survives. `size` and `inline` are gone: the component renders a Phosphor glyph and the .ds-spinner--sm/--lg/--inline classes size it.

renames.to: Stepper + StepperItem + StepperIndicator + StepperContent + StepperTitle + StepperDescription
renames.note: `circle` has no replacement — .ds-stepper--circle is still in the stylesheet and can be passed through className. There is no StepperSeparator: the connector is a ::after on the step.

renames.to: Timeline + TimelineItem + TimelineIndicator + TimelineContent + TimelineTitle + TimelineTime + TimelineDescription
renames.note: `status` becomes `tone` on the item, and data-state="completed"|"active" fills or outlines the indicator.

renames.to: Toolbar + ToolbarGroup + ToolbarButton + ToolbarLink + ToolbarInput + ToolbarSeparator
renames.note: Base UI's Toolbar: the strip is one tab stop with arrow-key navigation. `bordered` is gone (boxed by default) and ToolbarSpacer with it — the bar is width: fit-content.
KbdGroup chains keys into one chord.
Moves out of react/index.tsx into its own module and gains the six-tone axis; the fixed-yellow identity is now `tone="warning"`.

New: 0.11 shipped table.css with no React binding. Table + TableHeader + TableBody + TableFooter + TableRow + TableHead + TableCell + TableCaption. DataGrid is unaffected and stays the stateful table.
No replacement — the title/description pair needs no class, only a wrapper element.
An attribute rather than a class: .ds-page-header reads it through :has() to move its bottom rule, and it styles nothing itself.
Removed — derived from the tab slot's presence.
The <nav> root carries no class now; the <ol> is the styled element.
New — the current page, which 0.11 marked with aria-current alone.
New — the separator is its own presentational <li> rather than a ::after, so it flips for RTL and stays out of the neighbouring item's accessible name.
New — a collapsed middle of the trail.
Size is an attribute so a group can size its overflow count off its members with :has().
No longer also carries .ds-avatar.
Removed — the group reads its members' data-size.
Removed — the group reads its members' data-size.
New — bare initials inside .ds-avatar are no longer styled; they go in this slot.
New — the corner status dot.
Two elements now: .ds-progress is the wrapping row that also holds the label and value.
A sibling of the track inside .ds-progress, not a row above it.
New — the tone axis is six-wide now.
Add --icon for the tinted tile; --default leaves it bare.
New — groups the media, title and description and caps their width.
Now the wrapper around the title, time and description rather than the description itself.
Tone moves from the dot to the item; the state attribute is what fills the indicator with it. Same for is-info / is-warning / is-danger / is-neutral.
New — the supporting text under the title.
The source kept the row spacing a Tailwind literal for a tailwind-merge dedupe. Baked into timeline.css; override with this custom property on an item or on the list.
Now an <h3> over a <section> per day rather than a bare div.
No replacement — the date is a bare <time datetime> inside the heading.
States move from .is-success to .ds-agenda-event-status--success. Batch 7 replaces the span with a real <Status>.
No bespoke empty class: the agenda renders the system's empty state.
A page is a Button now — .ds-button, plus --icon for the square metric and --primary for the active page.
New — the <ul> the page items sit in.
New — the prev/next text, hidden below 640px.
New — the prev/next glyph, flipped for RTL.
Kept, but the bar is width: fit-content now, so the spacer only does anything on a toolbar widened past its content.
Removed — the bar is boxed by default, which is what --bordered opted into.
New parts.

New — the part grammar the composed <Table> renders. 0.11's .ds-table th/td, --hover, __num, __name and __row-action are PRESERVED alongside it: four files under examples/ plus docs read them, and no React component on either side would have re-classed them.
Kept for hand-written HTML, scoped `:not(svg)`. The React binding spins a glyph instead, and the rotation is shared.
The bare class is now the neutral tone. The 0.11 identity is the warning tone.
New parts.

0.11's status *panel* — the coloured head with a kicker, heading and subtitle. `Status` is now the source's inline dot-and-label indicator, and one barrel cannot export both under one name. `<ds-status>` is unchanged and still renders the panel, so no web-component consumer moves.
It could not stay as a deprecated alias: a type alias named `Status` in the barrel shadows the `Status` *component* for every consumer.

On Base UI, so a range is one control with two thumbs rather than two inputs kept in order by the caller. `.ds-range` — the native `<input type=range>` — is still defined in `slider.css` for hand-written HTML. To label a single-thumb Slider, use `aria-labelledby` (pointing at the label's own id) or `aria-label` — not `id` + a sibling `<FieldLabel htmlFor>` the way Checkbox/RadioGroupItem work. Base UI never routes the id down to the real, nested `<input>`.

Replaced by `FieldDescription` (neutral) and `FieldError` (`role="alert"`, so a validation message is announced when it appears — `FieldHint` was a bare span and never was). `.ds-field__hint` stays defined in `field.css` for hand-written HTML. `<FormField>` absorbs the swap: its own props are unchanged.
Composition replaces configuration. `clickable` survives as a prop, because it is what the whole card *is* — it carries the `tabIndex` and the `role` with it.
`rows` survives: `<ds-panel rows>` writes `ds-panel--rows` itself, so the modifier is a frozen contract.
The label is an element, which is what lets a field also carry a description, an error and an orientation.

The parts buy what a native `<select>` cannot render: a group label, a separator, an icon in a row, a checked indicator. `.ds-select` — the native wrapper — is still defined in `select.css` for hand-written HTML.
An addon can now sit above or below the control (`align="block-start"` / `"block-end"`), which a two-slot prop pair could not express.
The root is the box now, not a label around one. Pair it with a `<FieldLabel htmlFor>`; `indeterminate` is a real third state.
Same shape change as Checkbox: the root is the track, and its name is a `<Label htmlFor>` beside it.
Widened from four values to the same six every other status surface takes. `status` is still accepted and still maps.
Accepted and ignored since the set became Phosphor: filled geometry has no stroke to widen. Still accepted rather than removed, because removing it costs a caller a build for no gain.
Widened, not renamed: these narrowed to `primary | danger` while they were composed onto the incumbent Button. The second half of batches 1, 3 and 6's forward cross-batch imports.
The absorbed part is renamed into the frozen grammar: `__body` is what this system already called that region.
Renamed into the frozen BEM grammar `Card.js` and `docs/components.md` already taught.
Same rename. `__title` is what `<ds-panel title>` writes, so it is a contract and the other four follow it.

Declarations moved file, name unchanged. Four stylesheets override it by descent — `color-picker.css`, `time-picker.css`, `date-picker.css`, `date-range.css` — and all four win on specificity, so none of them moved.

renames.to: the same names, in checkbox.css / textarea.css / select.css / slider.css / input-group.css
renames.note: `form-controls.css` split seven ways and kept only the radio block. Every class name is unchanged; only the file it lives in moved. `.ds-field--error`, `.ds-field--success` and `.ds-field__hint` moved to `field.css`.
The agenda's status dot is a `<Status><StatusIndicator/>` now, so its six private tone rules left `agenda.css`. One status is one colour system-wide.
Lucide -> Phosphor. Every icon **name** is unchanged, so no `<Icon>` or `<ds-icon>` call moves; hand-written `<svg class="ds-icon">` does, because the wrapper attributes and the geometry both change.

A defect swap, not a rename of convenience. 0.11's Tooltip put role="tooltip" on a sibling span with no id and no aria-describedby on the trigger, and had no Escape dismissal. `<Tooltip label="Save" placement="bottom"><IconButton/></Tooltip>` becomes `<Tooltip><TooltipTrigger render={<IconButton aria-label="Save"/>}/><TooltipContent side="bottom">Save</TooltipContent></Tooltip>`. The trigger MUST carry its own accessible name: the popup is visual-only by design and wires no description. Pinned by site/tests/tooltip-regress.spec.ts.

Both grammars ship. The 0.11 pair is the CSS-only hover host and still works for hand-written HTML; the React <Tooltip> renders only the absorbed one. They share no class name, so no guard was needed.

renames.to: Sheet + SheetTrigger + SheetContent + SheetHeader + SheetTitle + SheetDescription + SheetFooter + SheetClose
renames.note: THE MERGE. 0.11's one Drawer did two jobs and the absorption splits it, so `placement` lands on Sheet, not on the new Drawer. `<Drawer open placement="right" heading="Filters" footer={…}>` becomes `<Sheet open><SheetContent side="right"><SheetHeader><SheetTitle>Filters</SheetTitle></SheetHeader>…<SheetFooter>…</SheetFooter></SheetContent></Sheet>`. Earned on a measured defect: 0.11 had no focus trap and no portal, so Tab walked out of an open drawer. Pinned by site/tests/drawer-regress.spec.ts.

The name survives but the component behind it does not. The 1.0 Drawer is the swipeable sheet — snap points, a swipe axis, an optional grab handle — and is uncontrolled by default. A 0.11 `<Drawer open placement>` call site must move to `Sheet` (row above); it will not fail to compile on `open` alone, so this is the one row worth grepping for by hand.

The 0.11 grammar is NOT removed — examples/components/drawer.html, kitchen-sink.html and the demo's files.js write it by hand and nothing re-classes them. Only .ds-drawer-overlay is shared between the two grammars, told apart by whether it wraps a `> .ds-drawer`.
Net-new file, css/components/sheet.css, imported after drawer.css.

renames.from: Kanban (items prop, seeded and then self-owned)
renames.note: A defect swap: 0.11 was 49 lines of HTML5 drag with zero ARIA and no keyboard path at all. The board is now a @dnd-kit lift/move/drop state machine — the grip is a real button, so Space lifts, arrows move, Space drops, Escape cancels. `items` is now genuinely CONTROLLED: passing it without `onItemsChange` pins every card. Seeding behaviour is `defaultItems`. `onMove` reports (itemKey, toColumnId) and fires only on a column change, not a reorder. Pinned by site/tests/kanban-regress.spec.ts.
Flat kebab, per #157's C2. The three committed readers are re-classed in this batch.
The column label now takes .ds-kanban-column-title rather than a bare span.
The drop-target highlight moves from `.is-over` to `[data-over]`, which is what dnd-kit sets.
Now a flex row of a grip and a `.ds-kanban-card-body`; hand-written content belongs in the body or it sits beside the grip.
Carried over from the 0.11 grammar rather than dropped: the source defines no meta part, and the re-classed fixtures needed somewhere to land.

Composition replacing configuration, the trade every applier in this migration makes. `variant` is the held stylesheet's own modifier — `<Skeleton variant="text"/>` becomes `<Skeleton className="ds-skeleton--text"/>`; `width`/`height` become `style`; `count={3}` becomes a map. skeleton.css is HELD (DataGrid renders .ds-skeleton--text), so every modifier a 0.11 call site used still exists. It also renders a <div> now, not a <span>, and carries no aria-hidden — mark the loading REGION with aria-hidden or role="status", which is what a screen reader actually needs.

Additive, no call site moves. `sidebar`'s two cherry-picks (#164 A3): `persist` remembers the collapsed state in a week-long cookie, `shortcut` binds Cmd/Ctrl+B to the toggle. Both default on and both are no-ops without a `sidebar`. The other 23 of sidebar's composition parts do not port.
recharts is now installed automatically with the package instead of requiring a separate `npm i recharts`. No import path changes.

Config becomes composition: items[] is gone, each row is an AccordionItem (its value is what defaultValue/value refers to) wrapping AccordionTrigger and AccordionContent. openMultiple replaces multiple; defaultValue/value is always an array (Value[]), whether or not openMultiple is on.

type becomes tone (neutral | info | success | warning | danger | critical, plus a variant axis: default | destructive). dismissible is gone: AlertDismiss renders the close button but is deliberately stateless — the caller holds whether the alert is dismissed and stops rendering it.

renames.from: SplitButton ({ children, onMain, variant, size, menu })
renames.to: SplitButton ({ children, onMain, variant, size, tone, disabled, menu, menuLabel })
renames.note: Same name, real rewrite: built on ButtonGroup + DropdownMenu now (was a hand-rolled popover with its own outside-click/Escape handling). menu takes DropdownMenuItem rows, not arbitrary nodes. Moved from react/components/ButtonExtras.tsx (retired) to react/components/split-button.tsx.

renames.from: Calendar ({ month, value, events, weekStartsOn, onSelectDate })
renames.note: react-day-picker underneath now (was a hand-rolled month grid). mode ("single" | "range" | "multiple") + selected/onSelect replace value/onSelectDate; defaultMonth replaces month. events is gone — a per-day marker is a components={{ DayButton: ... }} override composing CalendarDayButton, not a data prop.

Config becomes composition: filename is a CodeBlockFilename child inside CodeBlockHead, code/html move to CodeBlockBody. language is gone — there was never a real grammar behind it, and the source ships none either. CodeBlockCopyButton no longer takes children/label: it always renders its own check/copy Icon and manages its own "copied" state.
Compatible — the only row in the 28 with no prop change. Gains className.

renames.to: Combobox, ComboboxTrigger, ComboboxValue, ComboboxInput, ComboboxContent, ComboboxList, ComboboxItem, ComboboxGroup, ComboboxLabel, ComboboxCollection, ComboboxEmpty, ComboboxSeparator, ComboboxChips, ComboboxChip, ComboboxChipsInput, useComboboxAnchor
renames.note: Config becomes composition: options becomes items on the root plus ComboboxItem rows inside ComboboxContent/ComboboxList. allowCustom has no direct replacement. MultiSelect is the friendlier options/value wrapper over this component's multiple + chips mode, for the common case.

renames.to: Command, CommandDialog, CommandInput, CommandList, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandItem, CommandShortcut, CommandSeparator
renames.note: Renamed and decomposed onto cmdk. The flat commands[] (grouped by a group field, each with onRun) is gone — CommandGroup's heading restores the grouping, CommandItem takes onSelect instead of onRun. CommandDialog is the ⌘K popup shell (a Dialog underneath); Command on its own composes inline.

Renamed, on @tanstack/react-table now. columns is a real ColumnDef[] (accessorKey/header/cell) rather than { key, header, render }; rows is data. Drops the old custom keyboard-navigable grid entirely (no grid/gridcell roles, no roving tabindex, no arrow-key cell nav) — the source doesn't cover that axis at all; see corrections.md.

renames.from: DatePicker ({ defaultValue, min, max, placeholder }), DateLike
renames.note: DatePicker is Popover itself now; DatePickerTrigger/DatePickerContent are the parts it adds, composing a Calendar by hand inside. min/max are gone — bounding is Calendar's own disabled matchers ({ before }/{ after }). value is a real Date, not a DateLike (Date | string) — the type is retired with no replacement.

Same name, real rewrite: owns its own Calendar in mode="range" now. value is { from, to } (real Dates, to optional) instead of an ISO-string pair; min/max are gone, no bound replaces them. showTime adds a TimePicker for each end.
Compatible, but step changes units: minutes now, not seconds (step={15} where it used to be step={900}). Composed from DatePicker + TimePicker internally. Gains datePlaceholder.

renames.to: DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuPortal, DropdownMenuTrigger, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, DropdownMenuRadioItem, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuShortcut, DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuSubContent
renames.note: Renamed and decomposed. trigger becomes DropdownMenuTrigger's render prop; MenuItem's as polymorphism becomes DropdownMenuItem's render. MenuHeader -> DropdownMenuLabel, MenuDivider -> DropdownMenuSeparator. Does not share a class vocabulary with Menubar/ContextMenu (.ds-menu__* — those are unaffected, separately landed net-new).
Config becomes composition: hint/name/value are gone, FileUploadIcon/FileUploadTitle/FileUploadDescription are children instead. onFiles, accept, multiple, disabled are unchanged.

renames.to: Field, FieldSet, FieldLegend, FieldGroup, FieldContent, FieldLabel, FieldTitle, FieldDescription, FieldSeparator, FieldError
renames.note: Renamed and decomposed: label -> FieldLabel child, error -> FieldError child, hint -> FieldDescription child. data-invalid on Field itself replaces the error-truthy switch. The group mints no ids and reads no form library's state — htmlFor/id and aria-invalid stay the caller's to set, same as before.

Same name, quieter contract: size, strokeWidth and title are gone. Sizing is CSS (.ds-icon is 1em square, font-size drives it); an accessible name is role="img" + aria-label passed straight through, or aria-hidden for a decorative icon. Ported to reuse this repo's own larger icon-geometry catalogue (icons.tsx) rather than source's per-icon @phosphor-icons/react imports, to avoid a second copy of the same data.

Same name, dangerous one: onChange silently stops reporting selection under the new component (it renders correctly, so nothing errors). Everything else — options, value, defaultValue, placeholder, disabled — is unchanged. No per-option disabled any more; filter it out of options at the call site instead. No id — pair with a label via aria-labelledby/aria-label.

renames.to: NumberField, NumberFieldGroup, NumberFieldInput, NumberFieldDecrement, NumberFieldIncrement, NumberFieldScrubArea
renames.note: Renamed and decomposed onto Base UI's NumberField. min/max/step/value/defaultValue/onValueChange are unchanged; the steppers and the input are now composed children (NumberFieldGroup wraps NumberFieldDecrement/NumberFieldInput/NumberFieldIncrement) rather than baked in.

renames.to: Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent, PopoverHeader, PopoverTitle, PopoverDescription
renames.note: Config becomes composition: trigger -> PopoverTrigger child, title -> PopoverTitle child (inside PopoverContent), placement -> side/align on PopoverContent. arrow has no replacement. defaultOpen / open+onOpenChange are unchanged.

Radio is retired; RadioGroup keeps its name but options is gone — RadioGroupItem is one per option, composed as children, each drawing only the dot (no self-label, unlike the incumbent Radio). Pair each with a Field-wrapped FieldLabel/Label the same way any other bare control is. label.css's sibling rule updated to match (radio-group-item dropped from the self-labelling-control selector list).
onChange -> onValueChange. Gains shape ("default" | "star") and disabled. max/value/defaultValue/readOnly unchanged.

renames.from: StatCard ({ label, value, delta, deltaDir, animate })
renames.note: Config becomes composition: label/value/delta -> StatCardLabel/StatCardValue/StatCardDelta children, deltaDir -> direction on StatCardDelta, children (the spark slot) -> StatCardSpark wrapper. animate (count-up-on-mount tween) has no replacement — the source's version doesn't animate the figure.
Renamed only — value, defaultValue, onValueChange, placeholder, disabled, max are all unchanged.

renames.from: TimePicker ({ defaultValue: string, name, placeholder, step })
renames.to: TimePicker ({ defaultValue: TimeValue, picker, showSeconds }), TimeValue
renames.note: The value is { hours, minutes, seconds? } now, not a "HH:mm" string. name, placeholder and step (the quarter-hour-snap seconds prop) are gone with no replacement — there's no discrete step on the new dial/list pickers. Gains picker ("dial" | "list" | "none") and showSeconds.

renames.to: Toaster, toast, useToastManager, createToastManager, Toast, ToastProvider, ToastPortal, ToastViewport, ToastContent, ToastTitle, ToastDescription, ToastAction, ToastClose
renames.note: ToastProvider keeps its name but is now just the context provider — mount Toaster once at the app root instead (it wraps ToastProvider + the portal + viewport + list). Raise a toast with the standalone toast.add({ type, title, description }) manager, not useToast().show(). duration and children on the old ToastProvider have no replacement.

Config becomes composition: nodes[] is gone, a branch is a TreeItem (defaultOpen seeds it open) wrapping TreeItemTrigger + TreeItemContent, a childless node is a TreeLeaf. Drops the old custom roving-tabindex keyboard model entirely (no arrow-key expand/collapse) — the source's version is plain Collapsibles with no tree-specific keyboard layer; see corrections.md.

renames.to: SidebarProvider, Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarHeader, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupAction, SidebarGroupContent, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarInput, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuAction, SidebarMenuBadge, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuSkeleton, SidebarMenuSub, SidebarMenuSubButton, SidebarMenuSubItem, SidebarRail, SidebarSeparator, SidebarTrigger, useSidebar
renames.note: Renamed and decomposed — the near-total rewrite of the 28 (80 lines to 674, 23 exports). items[] with one level of nesting is gone; nesting is however many SidebarMenuSub levels a call site composes. isActive on SidebarMenuButton/SidebarMenuSubButton replaces active, same no-router-opinion as before.

Compatible. Gains label, nextLabel, backLabel, finishLabel. Composes Stepper's parts for the trail now rather than drawing its own — with no StepperSeparator between steps, since stepper.css's connector is a ::after with no separator element to render (see corrections.md).

notes.subject: SpeedDial
notes.note: The source composes its trigger onto its own eight-tone Button; that component holds until batch 7, so the trigger is this repo's IconButton and `tone` accepts only its two variants (`primary`, `danger`). Batch 7 re-wires it back and owes the row.

notes.subject: AutocompleteInput / AutocompleteClear
notes.note: The source composes onto its own compound InputGroup (InputGroupInput / InputGroupAddon / InputGroupButton); that component holds until batch 7, so these compose onto this repo's InputGroup (`after` slot) and IconButton. Batch 7 re-wires them back and owes the row.

notes.subject: context-menu
notes.note: The /docs/context-menu route documented `Dropdown` and the absence of a right-click menu. It now documents the real `ContextMenu`. Nothing a consumer imports changed name — `Dropdown` is unmoved and still documented at /docs/dropdown-menu — so this is not a rename row.

notes.subject: AttachmentAction
notes.note: The source composes onto its own eight-tone Button at variant="ghost" size="icon-xs"; that component holds until batch 7, so it composes onto this repo's IconButton — which requires `label`, since an icon-only action needs an accessible name the source's own ghost button never carried. Batch 7 re-wires it back and owes the row.

notes.subject: ThemeSwitcher
notes.note: All three variants are re-compositions. `segmented` was the source's own toggle-group (held) and is now this repo's Segmented: the cells carry a visible word beside the glyph rather than an icon-only aria-label, because Segmented takes a label node, and the source's sliding indicator goes with the toggle cells it was pitched against. `cycle` was the source's Button (batch 7) and is now IconButton. `dropdown` was the source's dropdown-menu (held) and is now Base UI's Menu wearing .ds-menu, the same re-wiring batch 1's menubar made. Batch 7 re-wires `cycle` back and owes the row.

notes.subject: Snippet
notes.note: The source composes the held code-block's `CodeBlockCopyButton`. This repo's CodeBlock baked the same button inline, so landing Snippet extracted it into a real export rather than duplicating the clipboard fallback. `CodeBlockCopyButton` is therefore new public surface on an incumbent, not a rename — CodeBlock's own props and markup are unchanged.

notes.subject: resizable, message-scroller
notes.note: Admit-CSS-only: the stylesheets ship, the React bindings do not (react-resizable-panels and @shadcn/react are not acquired, #156). Their registry entries declare `exports: []` and their pages print no import line — the .ds-resizable-* and .ds-message-scroller-* classes are the whole contract. Nothing a consumer of 0.x could import is affected, so no rename row is owed.

notes.subject: batch 2 dedupe exceptions
notes.note: Eight Tailwind literals kept as dedupe exceptions upstream are resolved into real declarations plus a modifier class for each consumer override: .ds-toc--static, .ds-toc-label--tight, .ds-toc-list--tight, .ds-toc-link--current, .ds-bubble-group--loose, .ds-message-scroller-content--tight, .ds-separator--auto, and resizable's h-full/w-full which become the group's own defaults. All are net-new names in a clean namespace, so no 0.x class is renamed.

notes.subject: Editable, FieldArray, IconButton
notes.note: The source composes these onto its own six-variant Button; that component holds until batch 7, so they compose onto this repo's Button and IconButton and `variant` accepts only `primary` and `danger`. Editable's three affordances gain a required accessible name in the process, since IconButton cannot ship without `label`. Batch 7 re-wires them back and owes the rows.

notes.subject: PhoneInput
notes.note: The source composes a five-part Base UI select (Select/SelectTrigger/SelectContent/SelectItem/SelectValue); that component holds until batch 7, so the five parts collapse onto this repo's native Select, which takes its options as a prop. Batch 7 re-wires it back and owes the row. The collapse is also what dissolves the batch's largest dedupe exception — nothing is literal on either side any more.

notes.subject: carousel, input-otp
notes.note: Stylesheet only: embla-carousel-react and input-otp are not acquired, so .ds-carousel-* and .ds-input-otp-* ship with no React binding, as resizable and message-scroller did in batch 2. No export is added or removed; a binding that renders the documented markup gets the look.

notes.subject: recharts
notes.note: recharts >= 3 becomes an optional peer dependency — optional the way react is, since the CSS-only bindings need neither. It is a peer rather than a dependency because a chart's children are written by the consumer (`<Bar>`, `<XAxis>` are imported from recharts directly), so two copies would put the children and the container on different recharts contexts and the plot would render empty. Batch 5's eight net-new charts add no dependency of their own.

notes.subject: the six --ds-chart-* tokens
notes.note: Unchanged, and still the ramp: a series with no colour in `config` takes the next slot. What changed is how a colour reaches a mark — `config` emits a per-chart `--color-<key>` custom property that the mark references, so a key carrying a space (a slice named "Closed won") is folded to a dash-safe name first.

notes.subject: AlertDialog, Carousel, Command, DataTable, Dialog, DropdownMenu, InputOTP, NumberField, Resizable, Sidebar, TagsInput, ToggleGroup
notes.note: Landed additively (#45) — new names, no incumbent uses the same one, so no rename row yet. Each is exported from the barrel and from its own `./react/*` subpath. Batch 13 (#46) removes the incumbent each one eventually replaces (DataGrid, Dropdown, NumberInput, TagInput, VerticalNav — the rest are net-new) and owes the actual rename rows then.

notes.subject: color-picker, command (the `Command` interface), file-upload, radio-group, split-button, stat-card, tabs, toast
notes.note: Landed (#45) but NOT re-exported from the barrel: each has a same-named export already there (`ColorPicker`, `CommandPalette`'s `Command` type, `FileUpload`, `RadioGroup`, `SplitButton`, `StatCard`, the inline `Tabs`/`Segmented`, `Toast`/`ToastProvider`), and `export *` from two modules sharing a name is a compile error. Reachable only via `./react/<name>` until batch 13 swaps the incumbent out and the barrel export moves over.

notes.subject: resizable
notes.note: Supersedes batch 2's note: react-resizable-panels is acquired (batch 11, #44) and `react/components/resizable.tsx` lands here. No longer admit-CSS-only — `Resizable`, `ResizablePanel`, `ResizablePanelGroup`, `ResizableHandle` are real exports now.

notes.subject: code-block, date-picker, date-range-picker, date-time-picker, time-picker, multi-select
notes.note: In #45's 26 but not landed: each transitively imports `calendar`, `icon` or `combobox`'s decomposed parts, which don't exist yet under those exact names — only the PascalCase incumbents (`Calendar`, `Icon`, `Combobox`) do, and TypeScript's cross-case-collision check (TS1149) blocks a same-spelled lowercase sibling from coexisting with one, exactly like the export collisions above but one layer earlier and with no subpath escape hatch (there's no file to put the subpath version in without the same clash). Blocked until batch 13 swaps `Calendar`/`Icon`/`Combobox` for real; see corrections.md.
